description: We are middle school students from Chile looking to learn more about the future of humanity in space and the software involved in this, and we want to discover how space missions work in the present to improve them in the future, as this can impact what influence mankind has in space. We also like artificial intelligence, maths and data analysis, and the way we apply them in various contexts, including space.
summary: We developed a simple to use web tool that allows the user to click on a point on the moon, view it's data, and find analogues to it in our sample location of Northern Africa (for testing). We included data relevant for a moon base, like the temperature, slope/topography and ice probability for our moon points.
details: Our project allows the user to click on a point on the moon to then see it's latitude and longitude. Then they can click the Get Moon Data button to get other relevant moon data, like topology or temperature. They can then click Find Analogs to run an algorithm written in Python that classifies the parameters by weight and returns the coordinates of the analog sites, with OSM map links to check them out! We used a JavaScript frontend with three.js, and a Python/Flask backend. For the parameters we considered temperature, Slope/Elevation and Radiation, and Ice Favorability Index (IFI) and Minerals to consider the point as a good location for a moon base.
dataRefs: NASA ODS REST API (LOLA and DIVINIER)
